MessageInvitation.texte:
Hi! I use Allezou so our kids can meet up outside: it's how we say when we're
heading to the park, and see the activities in Geneva's municipalities.

It's free, hosted in Switzerland, with no ads, and for kids we only enter a
first name.

Here's the link to join our circle “{cercle}”:
{lien}
It works until {date}.

What the site stores, and who can see it: {donnees}

Metadata.promesse: So our kids can meet up outside. Shared outings and the agenda for Geneva families.
Metadata.accroche: So our kids can meet up outside

Accueil.accroche: So our kids can meet up outside.
Accueil.presentation: Hi, I'm Michael. I'm a dad to two little girls at school in Petit-Lancy.
Accueil.constat: A park can be full of people without your child finding anyone they know there. They play for ten minutes, then come ask when you're going home. Their classmates might have been at the next park over, or already come and gone an hour earlier.
Accueil.mission: I created Allezou for exactly this: so our kids can enjoy playing outside again, surrounded by kids they love spending time with.

cercles.texte: You bring together the families your kids love spending time with: their class, the neighborhood. You invite them with a link, by WhatsApp or text message. Nothing you post ever leaves these circles.

sortir.texte: You pick a park from the list and the time you'll head home. Families in your circles see it right away. The outing disappears on its own once that time passes.

voir.texte: You see who's out right now, and join them with one tap if you feel like it.

agenda.texte: Activities for families in Geneva and its municipalities. Their websites are checked several times a day, so you don't have to watch anything yourself. You check off the ones you'll go to, and see who else from your circles will be there too.

notifications.titre: Get notified about what you care about
notifications.texte: You pick your own words: “pool,” “storytime,” “judo.” As soon as an activity containing one of them appears on the agenda, your phone lets you know. You can also ask to be told about every activity that requires registration, since waiting too long for those often means missing out.

installation.intro: Allezou is a website, not a real app you download from a store. Depending on your browser, it may offer to install itself for you. You can say yes: it's just a shortcut to this page that opens full-screen and saves you from signing in every time.

sansProposition.texte: Look for “Install app” in your browser's menu, usually in the top right.

iphone.texte: Tap the Share button at the bottom of the screen, then “Add to Home Screen.” It's also the only way to get notifications there.

Accueil.absencesIntro: An app built around children needs to say where it draws the line.

messagerie.texte: There's no chat thread, and no private messaging.

position.texte: You pick a place from a list. The app never asks your phone where you are.

historique.texte: An outing disappears 24 hours after it ends. No one can piece together where your family went last month.

inconnus.texte: You only see members of your circles. Joining an outing doesn't show you to anyone else.

publicite.texte: Your data doesn't go to anyone, and is never sold to anyone.

prenom.titre: About your kids: just a first name
prenom.texte: And nothing more: that's all Allezou knows about them.

Accueil.gratuitTexte: There's no company behind Allezou, and nothing costs anything. The servers are in Switzerland. The agenda fills itself in automatically from the websites of Geneva's municipalities.
Accueil.nePlusAfficher: Don't show this page again on this device
Accueil.lienDonnees: What Allezou stores, and who can see it

Compte.coparentTexte: Give it to the person raising the same kids. It's valid for 14 days and works only once. They'll then see the same first names you do.

Compte.langueTexte: Screens, emails, and notifications will speak to you in this language.
Compte.autreParentTexte: If you're raising these kids together, the other parent can have their own account and see the same first names. Each of you keeps your own circles and settings.

Compte.passkeyTexte: Save a passkey on this device, and next time you'll sign in the same way you unlock your phone: fingerprint, face, or passcode. None of that ever reaches us: your device keeps a private key it shares with no one, and we only ever see the public half. The email link is still there if you switch phones.
Compte.supprimerTexte: Your outings, settings, email address, and name disappear. Circles you created keep existing for their members. A child with only you as a parent is erased; if they have a second parent, that parent keeps them. This is permanent.
